about: The end-to-end scenarios for a DataPipe deployment, as data rather than prose. site/index.html renders its "What to check" list from this file, and the e2e-testbed skill in the datapipe repo drives it. Add `experiment`, `base` and `run` to each scenario's params to build a URL.

defaults.verifiedField: Each scenario, and each `knownIssues` entry (folded into its `summary`/`consequence`), carries a `verified` marker instead of a run log: `"live"` means its page/dashboard/storage expectations have been confirmed against a live deployment; `"code"` means they are derived from the handler and component source only, not yet confirmed live; `"partial"` means part is confirmed and part is not, with `verifiedNote` saying which part.
defaults.resultContract: Result contract SCHEMA 2. Read `document.documentElement.dataset.testbedSchema`, `.testbedStatus`, `.testbedTrialsCompleted` and `.testbedTrialsPlanned` (the `data-testbed-schema`, `data-testbed-status`, `data-testbed-trials-completed` and `data-testbed-trials-planned` attributes on `<html>`), plus the JSON text of `#testbed-result`, from the DOM. `window.__testbed` holds the same object, but a browser extension evaluating JavaScript in an isolated world may not see a page global -- prefer the DOM. Read `data-testbed-schema` FIRST -- a one-line DOM check, no JSON parse needed -- and fall back to the JSON's `schema` field if that attribute is absent, then to schema-1 behaviour if neither is present: a cached schema-1 page has no `ready` status (it reads `running` from load), no trial counter and no `source` on its requests, and every expectation below that names one of those has to fall back to the schema-1 behaviour.
defaults.statusMachine: ready -> running -> finished | failed, and ready -> aborted. `ready` means loaded, settings valid, waiting for the participant's first keypress -- BOTH pages sit there on "Press any key to start". `running` means the first trial has started. `failed` is also reachable straight from `ready` when the jsPsych page's breaksave pre-claim is refused.
defaults.startingARun: Both pages wait for a real keypress, and the first one after a navigation is often swallowed -- `space` does not work, `f` does. Wait for `data-testbed-status` to read `ready`; then, in SEPARATE tool calls, click the page body and send ONE `f`; then verify. VERIFY MEANS `data-testbed-status` HAS MOVED FROM `ready` TO `running` -- while it still reads `ready` the key did not land, so click and send again. `f` is also a valid trial response, so an extra keypress is harmless.
defaults.trialCounter: `trialsPlanned` is the `trials` parameter; `trialsCompleted` counts only the task's own trials and reaches `trialsPlanned` exactly on a clean finish. Instruction screens are NOT counted on either page, so the jsPsych page's stored CSV holds one row more than `trialsCompleted` (its instruction trial). Poll `data-testbed-trials-completed` to act at a given trial rather than timing it off the clock.

preconditions.experiment: A fresh experiment on the deployment under test, storing to Google Drive (new experiments cannot choose OSF). Record its ID.
preconditions.dataCollection: "Accept new data" ON, except where a scenario says otherwise.
preconditions.validation: LEAVE THE DEFAULTS ALONE -- no setup needed. A new experiment ships with validation ON and one required field, `trial_type` (create-experiment.ts: `useValidation ?? true`, `requiredFields ?? ["trial_type"]`). Both pages satisfy it: jsPsych writes `trial_type` itself from each plugin's `info.name`, and the plain-JavaScript page puts `trial_type: "letter-keyboard-response"` on every row. If a scenario is unexpectedly refused with 400 INVALID_DATA, this is where to look. `validation-failure` is the one scenario that omits the column on purpose.
preconditions.metadata: "Generate Psych-DS metadata" LOCKS PERMANENTLY once the experiment has data ("Locked because this experiment has collected data"). Decide before the first submission. With it on, raw files move from the folder root to data/raw/, derived CSVs appear beside them, and a submission that is not parseable CSV/JSON is refused with METADATA_ERROR.
preconditions.conditions: "Assign conditions in sequence" OFF by default; the condition scenarios switch it.
preconditions.base64: "Accept base64 file uploads" OFF by default; the base64 scenarios switch it.

ordering.rule: Run scenarios in `order`. A scenario that changes experiment-level state (`mutatesExperimentState`) affects every scenario after it, and one with `mustRunLast` must not run before the scenarios in its `runAfter` have met their `runAfterCondition`.
ordering.why: Switching "Accept new data" off for `closed-experiment` while an earlier session is still staged DESTROYS that session's recovery. The staging sweep re-checks the experiment before promoting anything (scheduled-staging-sweep.ts, "THE SECOND DOOR") and discards staged trials outright when `active` is false -- which can look like a recovery bug that does not exist.
ordering.alternative: Run `closed-experiment` on a second throwaway experiment instead, and the ordering constraint goes away.

timingFacts.sweepCron: */5 (staging sweep and upload retry every tick; pending recovery on the :00/:15/:30/:45 slots; mail retry on :00/:10/...)
timingFacts.note: A recovered session is QUEUED by the sweep, not uploaded by it. queue-upload.ts gives an entry with no provider error code nextRetryAt = now + 1 hour, and the retry worker runs on */5 -- so a partial file reaches storage roughly 65-75 minutes after the participant dropped out, not 15. A recovered session is typically queued about ten to fifteen minutes after the tab closes (the abandonment grace period plus the next 5-minute sweep). For that hour the dashboard's queue panel lists it as "Waiting to be stored" -- not a failed upload -- with retryCount 0 and lastAttemptAt null. That is expected, not a bug.
timingFacts.whenTheClockStarts: For an abandoned tab, at the socket drop -- an open tab counts as live. For a refused final submission, datapipe-client stamps the session abandoned IMMEDIATELY (packages/client/src/session.ts, `close({submitted:false})`), so the clock starts at the refusal; whether @jspsych/extension-pipe does the same is not verified, so close the tab promptly afterwards either way. The 24-hour `expiresAt` is the backstop behind both.
timingFacts.observedPageRates: jsPsych page with auto=1: 1.1-1.7 s per trial. Vanilla page with auto=1: 400 ms per trial. A /api/data call that writes to Drive: 2-4.5 s. Size any "act at trial N" step off the FAST end, and add the cost of the driver's own polling -- a browser-extension tool call costs a few seconds, so a 5 s poll cadence can overshoot by 20-30 s.

knownIssues.summary: On Google Drive, one `.psychds-ignore` file accumulates per successful upload rather than one per experiment, so N uploads leave N copies. metadata-derived-upload.ts dedupes on the provider's NAME_CONFLICT, and Drive permits duplicate names, so the dedupe never fires.
knownIssues.consequence: Never assert on the TOTAL number of files in the folder. Count the files matching this scenario's filename stem instead. A pre-existing DataPipe bug, not a testbed one.

knownIssues.summary: A submission refused with 400 METADATA_ERROR keeps its pending Cloud Storage copy on purpose (api-data.ts: "scheduled-pending-recovery salvages it later instead of losing it outright"). METADATA_ERROR means metadata generation failed, not that the participant's data was refused, and the policy is never to destroy raw data over it.
knownIssues.consequence: Within the next pending-recovery slot (:00/:15/:30/:45, for entries older than ~15 minutes) a queue entry appears for that filename. EXPECT it. Do not flag it. Its failureReason is "Kept after a metadata failure (raw data stored without Psych-DS files)" on a current deployment (api-data.ts labels the pending copy, scheduled-pending-recovery.ts reads the label); a deployment that predates that labeling shows the generic "Recovered from interrupted upload (server restart or memory limit)" instead -- accept either, and say which you saw. On a current deployment the dashboard's queue panel shows the entry as "Waiting to be stored", not "Retrying": it has not failed. A kept copy is visible in the queue for only about 5 minutes before its own first storage attempt; miss that window and the only evidence left is the rejections panel.

knownIssues.summary: The dashboard shows the rejections panel only while the upload queue is empty.
knownIssues.consequence: Any `expectDashboard` line about an error-panel entry can only be checked when nothing is queued. After a recovery scenario has queued a partial, that is roughly 1 h 5 min away -- the entry's first storage attempt is nextRetryAt, an hour after it was queued. Check the rejections panel BEFORE running the recovery scenarios, or use `GET /api/queuestatus` and the endpoint response codes as the evidence instead.

knownIssues.summary: metadata-block.ts returns `{...MESSAGES.METADATA_ERROR, message: errorMessage}` -- it overrides the message with the specific failure text, so the wire message for METADATA_ERROR is not the string in api-messages.ts.
knownIssues.consequence: Assert on the `error` code. Never on `message`, for any endpoint.

knownIssues.summary: Loading the jsPsych page starts a session before any trial runs, so a page opened and navigated away from leaves a live-session row behind until the sweep clears it.
knownIssues.consequence: Never assert on the NUMBER of sessions in progress. Match rows by this scenario's `run` id.

scenarios.title: Clean finish
scenarios.description: jsPsych with save-as-you-go. The dashboard shows one session in progress with a running time while you work; it disappears when you finish, and exactly one file lands in storage.
driverActions: Start the run as `defaults.startingARun` describes: wait for `ready`, click, send one `f`, confirm the status has moved to `running`.

expectPage.trials: trialsCompleted === trialsPlanned === 20 -- the run reached the end rather than being cut short
notes: expect an `extension-pipe:` note only if something degraded
a note saying sessionId is null on this page by design

expectDashboard: While running: a "Sessions in progress" panel with a row reading "In progress" and a "Running for" value. Match the row, not the count.
Within ~30 s of the page reporting finished: that row is gone.
No new queue entry for this scenario's filename.

expectStorage.countBy: files matching this scenario's filename stem; ignore `.psychds-ignore` and the derived Psych-DS copies
expectStorage.naming: testbed-<run>-<stamp>-<pid>.csv, exactly the name in the result's filenames
expectStorage.completeness: complete: a header row, the instruction trial, and one row per trial
expectStorage.location: experiment folder root, or data/raw/ with metadata on (plus a derived subject-..._data.csv beside it)

timing.pageRun: ~30 s (observed 1.1-1.7 s per trial with auto=1)
timing.checkDashboardAfter: during the run, and again ~30 s after it finishes
timing.checkStorageAfter: ~30 s after the page reports finished

scenarios.description: With save-as-you-go off there is one submission at the end, as before incremental upload existed. One file, and no in-progress row at any point.
driverActions: Start the run as `defaults.startingARun` describes.
expectDashboard: No row for this scenario in "Sessions in progress" at any point -- nothing calls /api/session.
No queue entry.

expectStorage.location: experiment folder root, or data/raw/ with metadata on

timing.checkStorageAfter: ~30 s after the page reports finished

scenarios.title: Ended early
scenarios.description: Set `abort` below the trial count and the experiment stops as a failed attention check would. The data is still submitted — the behaviour a save trial never had, because an aborted timeline never reaches one.
driverActions: Start the run as `defaults.startingARun` describes.

expectPage.trials: trialsCompleted === 5, trialsPlanned === 20 -- the clearest single assertion that the abort fired where it was told to
notes: a note reading "timeline ended early at trial 5 of 20"

expectDashboard: No row for this scenario afterwards; no new error-panel entry; no queue entry.

expectStorage.countBy: files matching this scenario's filename stem
expectStorage.naming: the name in the result's filenames
expectStorage.completeness: complete for what ran: 5 trial rows, not 20
expectStorage.location: experiment folder root, or data/raw/ with metadata on

timing.checkStorageAfter: ~30 s after the page reports finished

scenarios.title: Plain JavaScript, streaming
scenarios.description: The same recovery behaviour with no framework at all — an in-progress row while it runs, one file at the end. This was impossible until the staging client moved out of the jsPsych plugin.
driverActions: Start the run as `defaults.startingARun` describes: wait for `ready`, click the page body, send a single `f` in a SEPARATE call, and confirm `data-testbed-status` has moved to `running` before waiting on anything.

expectPage.sessionId: null at `ready` (the round trip has not landed yet), a non-empty string once it does -- this page, unlike the jsPsych one, can report it, as soon as it is set rather than only at the end

requests.label: session
requests.ms: time until the public sessionId property became non-empty, to the nearest 100 ms -- inferred, not read off the wire; see README's `requests` section

requests.label: final-save
requests.ms: a real duration; the page issued this one itself

notes: a note saying the `session` entry's status is reconstructed from the client's outcome, not observed on the wire

expectDashboard: While running: a row for this scenario reading "In progress".
After finishing: that row is gone.

expectStorage.countBy: files matching this scenario's filename stem
expectStorage.naming: the name in the result's filenames
expectStorage.location: experiment folder root, or data/raw/ with metadata on

timing.pageRun: ~8 s after the first keypress (observed 400 ms per trial)
timing.checkStorageAfter: ~30 s after the page reports finished

scenarios.verifiedNote: The page's requests (session, final-save) and the stored file are confirmed live, including that `sessionId` is captured as soon as `/api/session` lands rather than only at the end. The live-session dashboard row has not been confirmed for this scenario.

scenarios.title: Plain JavaScript, uncompressed body
scenarios.description: The same run with gzip off, so the submission goes through the hosting layer as a plain JSON body. Worth running alongside the compressed one because gzip and the hosting rewrite are the two things in front of `/api/data` that can each break on their own.
driverActions: Start the run as `defaults.startingARun` describes.
expectDashboard: Identical to vanilla-streaming.

expectStorage.countBy: files matching this scenario's filename stem
expectStorage.naming: the name in the result's filenames
expectStorage.completeness: complete, the same shape as the gzipped run
expectStorage.location: experiment folder root, or data/raw/ with metadata on

timing.checkStorageAfter: ~30 s after the page reports finished

scenarios.title: Duplicate rejection
scenarios.description: On the plain JavaScript page, sending the same file a second time is refused.
driverActions: Start the run as `defaults.startingARun` describes. `resubmit=1` presses "Send the same file again" itself; without it, click that button by hand.
expectDashboard: A new rejections-panel entry with the code FILE_EXISTS. Assert on the code, not the message. The panel is only rendered while the upload queue is empty -- see knownIssues.

expectStorage.countBy: files matching this scenario's filename stem -- the second request must not add a copy or overwrite the first
expectStorage.naming: the name in the result's filenames
expectStorage.location: experiment folder root, or data/raw/ with metadata on

timing.checkStorageAfter: ~30 s after the page reports finished

scenarios.verifiedNote: The refusal itself (400 FILE_EXISTS on resubmit) is confirmed live. The rejections-panel entry and the stored-file count have not been confirmed.

scenarios.title: Data that fails validation
scenarios.description: The plain JavaScript page leaves `trial_type` off every row, so the submission fails the validation rules a new experiment ships with. DataPipe refuses it with `INVALID_DATA` and stores nothing — and, unlike a metadata failure, keeps no copy to recover later.
driverActions: Nothing on the dashboard. This scenario exercises the DEFAULT validation settings, so do not change them.
Start the run as `defaults.startingARun` describes.
`stream=0` on purpose: api-data.ts deliberately leaves staged trials alone on INVALID_DATA, so a streamed run here would leave a recoverable session behind and turn this into a deferred scenario.

expectPage.trials: trialsCompleted === trialsPlanned === 5. `failed` is about the SUBMISSION, not the run: every trial ran, and the counter is how you tell the two apart.
notes: a note reading "failvalidation: `trial_type` is omitted from every row on purpose"

expectDashboard: A new rejections-panel entry with the code INVALID_DATA. Only visible while the upload queue is empty -- see knownIssues.
No queue entry, now or later.

expectStorage.completeness: nothing is written, and nothing appears later either: the useValidation block in api-data.ts runs BEFORE persistPending, so no pending copy exists for the recovery sweep to find. That is the contrast with a METADATA_ERROR refusal, which does leave one -- see knownIssues.

timing.checkStorageAfter: n/a -- but re-check at the next :00/:15/:30/:45 slot that NOTHING was queued

scenarios.title: Abandoned tab
scenarios.description: Close the tab half-way. Within seconds the dashboard row reads `Connection lost — may resume`; after 10 minutes, `Stopped — being recovered`; the sweep then queues the staged trials, and the `.partial.json` reaches storage about an hour later, not within 15 minutes.
driverActions: Start the run as `defaults.startingARun` describes, and do not go on until `data-testbed-status` reads `running`.
Read the result and KEEP the first filename FIRST -- it is unrecoverable once the tab is gone, and it is the only way to recognise the partial later.
Poll `data-testbed-trials-completed` about every 5 s. Close the tab when it reaches about half of `data-testbed-trials-planned` (~60). Do NOT time this off the clock.
Note the wall-clock time of the close: the recovery clock starts at the socket drop. An open tab counts as live.
scenarios.sizingNote: trials is 120, not 60, on purpose. At the FAST end of the measured pace (1.1 s/trial) 60 trials finish in ~66 s, so half-way arrives at ~33 s and leaves only ~33 s of margin -- less than a poll-and-close cycle of extension tool calls reliably fits in, and a run can finish on its own before the tab is closed. At 120 trials the run lasts 132-204 s, half-way arrives at 66-102 s, and there is 66-102 s left afterwards: even a 30 s overshoot closes the tab around trial 87 of 120, still plainly partial. A 5 s poll cadence is then comfortable, and the cost is ~2 minutes of waiting.

expectPage.trials: trialsCompleted is roughly half of trialsPlanned (~60 of 120) and MUST be less than trialsPlanned -- if it reached it, the run finished and this scenario did not happen. Record the exact value, but expect the queue entry's "Recovered from an abandoned session (N trials)" to be a FEW LESS than it, not equal: datapipe-client only flushes a trial to staging once flushEveryNTrials trials are buffered or flushIntervalMs has elapsed (10 and 10000ms on datapipe-test), so up to flushEveryNTrials-1 trials counted in trialsCompleted can still be unflushed, and lost, when the tab dies. Assert N is in [trialsCompleted - (flushEveryNTrials - 1), trialsCompleted], never trialsCompleted exactly.
notes: The page never reaches a terminal status: the tab is gone. The last status read before closing must be "running" -- not `ready`, which only means the start key never landed.
sessionId is null on this page by design -- extension-pipe 0.2.0 exposes no public way to read it. The run says so itself in `notes`.

expectDashboard: Within seconds of the tab closing: the row for this scenario reads "Connection lost — may resume".
About 10-12 minutes later: "Stopped — being recovered".

Then the row disappears and a queue entry appears with failureReason "Recovered from an abandoned session (N trials)", status pending, retryCount 0, lastAttemptAt null, nextRetryAt one hour out. N is expected to be a FEW LESS than the trialsCompleted you read before closing -- see `expectPage.trials` above -- not equal to it.

The queue panel lists it under the kind "Waiting to be stored", in a plain neutral panel with no coloured edge -- nothing has failed. Do not assert on the panel's column headers or row sub-lines; see knownIssues.

expectStorage.countBy: files matching `<this scenario's filename stem>-<8 hex>.partial.json`
expectStorage.naming: <submitted filename without its extension>-<8 hex characters>.partial.json. The hash suffix is ALWAYS there -- partialFilenameFor derives it from the session id, not from a name collision.
expectStorage.completeness: partial: only the trials staged before the tab closed
expectStorage.location: experiment folder root, or data/raw/ with metadata on

timing.pageRun: ~70-105 s to half-way at 120 trials, then closed
timing.checkDashboardAfter: immediately, at ~11 min, and at ~14 min
timing.checkStorageAfter: 65-75 minutes after the tab was closed

scenarios.deferredNote: Re-open the folder 75 minutes after the tab was closed and look for one *.partial.json matching this scenario's filename stem. Until then `GET /api/queuestatus?experimentID=<id>` is better evidence than the dashboard panel: it shows retryCount and lastAttemptAt. A queue entry that has never been attempted is the expected state, not a failure.
scenarios.verifiedNote: The live-session row transitions ("Connection lost — may resume" then "Stopped — being recovered"), the queue entry's appearance, its fields (failureReason, retryCount 0, lastAttemptAt null, nextRetryAt = createdAt + 60 min), and the queue panel's neutral "Waiting to be stored" treatment are all confirmed live. The deferred storage check -- the `.partial.json` actually landing in Drive ~65-75 minutes later -- has never been confirmed to complete.

scenarios.title: Failed final submission
scenarios.description: The page claims the filename first, so DataPipe refuses the real submission as a duplicate. The log shows the save failed, and the staged trials come back later as a `.partial.json` under a hash-suffixed name.
driverActions: Open the URL. The pre-claim runs BEFORE the timeline, while the status already reads `ready`, so wait for the `preclaim` request to appear in the result rather than sending a key straight away.

If the pre-claim is refused the page stops with status "failed" and a note instead of running -- `ready` goes straight to `failed` with trialsCompleted 0. That is a FAIL of the scenario, and the note says which code came back.
Otherwise start the run as `defaults.startingARun` describes and let it reach the end.

After the final save is refused, CLOSE THE TAB promptly. datapipe-client stamps the session abandoned at the refusal, but whether extension-pipe does the same is unverified; closing removes the doubt.
Note the wall-clock time of the refusal.

expectPage.trials: trialsCompleted === trialsPlanned === 20. trialsCompleted 0 with status failed means the PRE-CLAIM was refused and no timeline ran -- a different outcome, and a FAIL.

expectDashboard: A new rejections-panel entry with the code FILE_EXISTS -- visible only while the upload queue is empty, so check it BEFORE the partial is queued.
Within about 15 minutes of the refusal: a queue entry for `<stem>-<8 hex>.partial.json`, kind "Waiting to be stored".

expectStorage.countBy: files matching this scenario's filename stem: the pre-claim file, and later the -<8 hex>.partial.json
expectStorage.naming: the pre-claim file under the run's own filename, plus <stem>-<8 hex>.partial.json holding the staged trials
expectStorage.completeness: the pre-claim file holds one placeholder row, not data; the partial holds the real trials
expectStorage.location: experiment folder root, or data/raw/ with metadata on
expectStorage.note: api-data.ts deliberately does NOT discard staging on a duplicate-filename refusal -- that is what makes the partial recoverable. It DOES discard if the experiment is switched off before the sweep gets there; see `ordering`.

timing.checkDashboardAfter: immediately, and again ~15 min after the refusal
timing.checkStorageAfter: the pre-claim file immediately; the partial 65-75 minutes after the refusal

scenarios.deferredNote: Re-check the folder ~75 minutes after the refusal for the .partial.json. The pre-claim file is there straight away and is not the thing under test. Do NOT switch data collection off before this session's partial is visible in /api/queuestatus.
scenarios.verifiedNote: The refusal sequence (pre-claim 201, then final-save 400 FILE_EXISTS) is confirmed live. The deferred recovery check -- the `-<8 hex>.partial.json` reaching storage after the refusal -- has never been confirmed to complete; see the `ordering` rule about closing an experiment before a recovery scenario's partial is queued.

scenarios.title: Plain JavaScript, conditions
scenarios.description: With `Request a condition` ticked, the log shows the assigned number and the run proceeds normally.
driverActions: Switch "Assign conditions in sequence" ON and set "How many conditions?" to 2. Click the visible switch track, not the hidden checkbox, and wait for the "Saved" badge.
Start the run as `defaults.startingARun` describes. The condition is requested before the page is ready, so `condition` is already filled in while the status still reads `ready`.
Run it twice to see the sequence advance.

expectPage.condition: an integer in 0..n-1; two runs in a row give 0 then 1, since assignment is sequential and wraps
notes: a note saying the `condition` and `session` entries' status is reconstructed from datapipe-client's return value/outcome, not observed on the wire

expectDashboard: Nothing specific; the condition counter is not surfaced in the UI.

expectStorage.countBy: files matching this scenario's filename stem
expectStorage.naming: the name in the result's filenames
expectStorage.location: experiment folder root, or data/raw/ with metadata on

timing.checkStorageAfter: ~30 s after the page reports finished

scenarios.verifiedNote: Sequential condition assignment (0, then 1, wrapping) is confirmed live, including via a direct `/api/condition` probe. The stored file has not been confirmed for this scenario.

scenarios.title: Plain JavaScript, condition assignment switched off
scenarios.description: Switch condition assignment off on the dashboard and run again: the page reports that `getCondition` threw and refuses to start, rather than running an unassigned participant.
driverActions: Switch "Assign conditions in sequence" OFF and wait for the "Saved" badge.

Open the URL. No keypress is needed -- the page stops before it asks for one, so `data-testbed-status` goes `ready` to `aborted` and never reads `running`. Do not wait for `running` here; poll for a terminal status.

expectPage.serverSide: POST /api/condition answers 400 with error CONDITION_ASSIGNMENT_NOT_ACTIVE. The page cannot see the raw response, but the `condition` entry's status is parsed out of datapipe-client's thrown error message, which embeds the real HTTP status -- confirm the code with the direct probe in the skill's endpoint table if it matters.

expectDashboard: A new rejections-panel entry with the code CONDITION_ASSIGNMENT_NOT_ACTIVE. Only visible while the upload queue is empty.

scenarios.title: Base64 upload
scenarios.description: The plain JavaScript page sends a small valid base64 payload to `/api/base64`, which now runs inside the same consolidated function as `/api/data`. The decoded file lands alongside the run's data file.
driverActions: Switch "Accept base64 file uploads" ON first. Without it the endpoint answers 400 BASE64DATA_COLLECTION_NOT_ACTIVE before it ever looks at the payload.
Start the run as `defaults.startingARun` describes.
expectDashboard: No new rejections-panel entry.

expectStorage.countBy: files matching this scenario's filename stem
expectStorage.naming: the data file, plus <stem>.b64.txt holding the decoded text "testbed base64 payload"
expectStorage.location: the data file follows the metadata layout; the base64 file ALWAYS goes to the folder root -- /api/base64 does not apply the Psych-DS layout, and it runs no metadata block, so it is unaffected by METADATA_ERROR

timing.checkStorageAfter: ~30 s after the page reports finished

scenarios.verifiedNote: The `/api/base64` endpoint and file placement (folder root, unaffected by the Psych-DS layout) are confirmed live via a direct probe. The page-driven flow -- running trials, then the page's own base64 request -- has not been exercised.

scenarios.title: Base64 upload, invalid payload
scenarios.description: The same path with something that is not base64 at all. The endpoint refuses it with `INVALID_BASE64_DATA` and the run's own data file is unaffected.
driverActions: "Accept base64 file uploads" must still be ON: the active check runs BEFORE the validity check, so with it off this scenario returns the wrong code and proves nothing.
Start the run as `defaults.startingARun` describes.
expectDashboard: A new rejections-panel entry with the code INVALID_BASE64_DATA. Only visible while the upload queue is empty.

expectStorage.countBy: files matching this scenario's filename stem -- the data file only, no .b64.txt
expectStorage.location: experiment folder root, or data/raw/ with metadata on

timing.checkStorageAfter: ~30 s after the page reports finished

scenarios.verifiedNote: The endpoint refusal (400 INVALID_BASE64_DATA, refused before any provider write) is confirmed live via a direct probe. The page-driven flow has not been exercised.

scenarios.title: Brief dropout
scenarios.description: Go offline for about 30 seconds mid-run, then back online, and finish. The dashboard row flips to `Connection lost — may resume` and back to `In progress`; you get one complete file and no partial.
driverActions: Start the run as `defaults.startingARun` describes, then let `data-testbed-trials-completed` reach about 10 before doing anything else -- a fixed 10-second wait is not the same thing, and on a slow first paint it is not even a started run.
Put the browser offline for 30 seconds: DevTools network throttling, the OS network toggle, or Playwright's context.setOffline(true).
Go back online and let the run finish.

expectPage.trials: trialsCompleted === trialsPlanned === 200, including the trials recorded while offline
notes: an `extension-pipe:` note about a failed flush during the offline window is expected, not a failure

expectDashboard: During the offline window: the row for this scenario reads "Connection lost — may resume".
After reconnecting: back to "In progress" (the reconnect slot heals the disconnect stamp).
After finishing: no row for this scenario, and no queue entry.

expectStorage.countBy: files matching this scenario's filename stem -- and confirm there is NO .partial.json for it
expectStorage.naming: the name in the result's filenames
expectStorage.completeness: complete, including the trials recorded while offline
expectStorage.location: experiment folder root, or data/raw/ with metadata on

timing.checkDashboardAfter: during the offline window and again after reconnecting
timing.checkStorageAfter: ~30 s after the page reports finished
timing.note: The offline window must be under 10 minutes or the sweep will treat the session as abandoned.

scenarios.automationNote: The Chrome extension cannot throttle or disable the network, so an agent driving that extension cannot run this. No URL parameter was added to fake it: what is under test is the Realtime Database's own disconnect-and-heal path, and a page-level simulation would exercise neither the onDisconnect stamp nor the reconnect slot that clears it -- it would prove nothing while looking like it had. A Playwright job CAN run it with context.setOffline(true), which makes it the one non-`full` scenario worth putting in a headless job.

scenarios.title: Closed experiment
scenarios.description: Switch data collection off and run the jsPsych test: no session is started and the final submission is refused with `DATA_COLLECTION_NOT_ACTIVE`.
driverActions: STOP. Confirm first that every recovery-dependent scenario's partial is already QUEUED -- `GET /api/queuestatus?experimentID=<id>` must list an entry for `abandoned-tab` and for `failed-final-submission`. Switching collection off before that DESTROYS them.
Switch "Accept new data" OFF and wait for the "Saved" badge.
Start the run as `defaults.startingARun` describes and let it run to the end.
Switch "Accept new data" back ON afterwards if anything else follows.

expectPage.trials: trialsCompleted === trialsPlanned === 5 -- the participant's run is unaffected; only the submission is refused
notes: a `datapipe:` note that the session was not started; the page cannot see /api/session's status code itself

expectDashboard: No row for this scenario in "Sessions in progress" at any point.

New rejections-panel entries with the code DATA_COLLECTION_NOT_ACTIVE (logged twice: once by /api/session, once by /api/data). The panel is hidden while anything is queued, and by this point in the order the recovery scenarios' partials usually are -- use GET /api/queuestatus and the page's own request statuses as the evidence instead.
scenarios.mutatesExperimentState: turns "Accept new data" OFF -- and while it is off the staging sweep DISCARDS any still-staged session
scenarios.runAfterCondition: each of those scenarios' partials is visible as a queue entry in GET /api/queuestatus?experimentID=<id>
